transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been doing some things that are… not really like me. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s been worrying me.

Like, I’ve walked out in the middle of work deployments, which I would never normally do, and I’ve been driving around late at night with no real plan. It scares me a little, honestly. I’ve always handled stress pretty responsibly, so this feels off.
Have you been acting on impulse when you do these things, like walking out of work or driving around late at night?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I’m not trying to be reckless on purpose, but in those moments I just kind of… go.

Like walking out during deployments, or getting in the car late at night with no real plan. That’s not how I’ve ever handled stress before, and it scares me a little. Does that make sense?
How have you been feeling emotionally when you act on these impulses?

Usually I tell myself I’m just stressed, but… emotionally, it’s like fear and shame get really loud all at once. Even on quiet days, I kind of feel it sitting in my chest, like I should’ve handled everything better.

And when I act on those impulses, it’s not that I’m trying to cause trouble. It feels more like… if I don’t move or get away, something bad could happen. I know that may not sound totally rational, but that’s how it feels in the moment.
Have you been experiencing any difficulties in your personal relationships recently?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I’m still trying to keep things together, so I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart.

But at home, my husband has said it feels like I’m barely present anymore. That was hard to hear. And at work… my last performance review was the first time anyone told me I was missing key handoffs, leaving meetings abruptly, making the team work around me.

I know that’s more work than personal, but I guess it’s all connected. I don’t want to be that person for people.
Have you always been someone who acts on impulse, or is this something that's changed for you recently?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve always tried to be pretty controlled, especially with work. I’m not someone who just walks out in the middle of something important.

That’s part of why I came in, honestly. I’ve started doing things that scare me a little, like leaving during deployments or getting in the car late at night with no plan. And that’s just… not how I’ve ever handled stress before. I don’t know if I’m explaining that right.
How long have you been noticing these impulsive behaviors in yourself?

I think… it’s been a little over a year now. Since that late-night cutover incident, really. So maybe about 13 months?

I kept thinking it was just a rough patch and I’d get back to normal, but it’s been long enough that I probably shouldn’t keep brushing it off.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when you're acting on these impulses?

I don’t… I don’t think so. Not in the sense of watching myself from outside my body, no.

Sometimes afterward I’ll think, “Why did I do that?” or it feels a little unreal that I acted that way, but while it’s happening I’m still… me, I guess. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you experienced any traumatic events in your past?

I’m… not sure how to answer that. I don’t really think of my past that way, I guess.

Nothing that I’ve ever labeled as “traumatic,” at least not comfortably. I mean, I know people go through much worse, so I don’t want to overstate anything. Are you asking about things like accidents or violence, or more… stressful work events?
Can you tell me more about what you mean by not labeling anything in your past as traumatic, is there something specific that you're hesitant to talk about?

I guess there is something specific, yeah. I’m just… I don’t like calling it traumatic, because that sounds dramatic, and I don’t want to make it seem bigger than it was.

But I do avoid parts of it. Like at work, I’ll take the long way around the building so I don’t have to pass that area, and I avoid that floor whenever I can. And if people start talking about the contractor or the cutover, I kind of shut the conversation down or find a reason to leave.

I know that probably sounds like avoidance. I’m not trying to be difficult—I just don’t really want to go back into it if I don’t have to.
Can you tell me more about the late-night cutover incident you mentioned earlier?

I’m sorry, I don’t think I can give you much more detail than what I already said. I know I mentioned it, but I’m still kind of… vague on how to talk about it without making it sound worse than it was.

It was a work thing, late at night, and it had to do with that area and the cutover. That’s really about as specific as I feel comfortable being right now, if that’s okay. I’m not trying to avoid your question exactly—I just don’t know how much is useful to say.
Do you ever feel disconnected from yourself or your surroundings when you're not acting on impulses?

I’m not sure. I don’t think so, not in a way I would know how to name.

Sometimes I might sort of zone out or feel a little distant if I’m stressed, but I’m not sure that’s what you mean. It doesn’t feel like I’m outside my body or anything dramatic like that. Maybe I just get quiet or go on autopilot a bit.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Did you often get into trouble or act out when you were a teenager?

Not really, no. I mean, I wasn’t perfect, but I don’t remember being the kind of teenager who was always in trouble or acting out.

I was more… I don’t know, I tried to keep my head down and do what I was supposed to do. Maybe I had normal teenage moods or disagreements, but nothing that I’d think of as a pattern. Is that what you mean?
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or spaced out when you're not acting on impulses?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I might get distracted or kind of go quiet sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m in a daze exactly.

Maybe I’m not recognizing it the way you mean it, though. When you say spaced out, do you mean like losing track of what’s happening around me, or just feeling kind of mentally checked out?
Do you ever feel like you're not really yourself when you're acting on these impulses?

I don’t think I’d put it that way, no. When I do something impulsive, I might feel embarrassed afterward or wonder why I did it, but in the moment it still feels like me, I guess.

I’m not sure if that’s the kind of “not yourself” you mean. I don’t feel like a different person takes over or anything like that.
Did you have any problems with rules or authority figures when you were younger?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I tried to be respectful, especially with teachers and adults. I wasn’t someone who was getting suspended or arguing with authority all the time.

I probably had moments where I didn’t like being told what to do, like any kid, but nothing major that I can think of. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Did you have any significant behavioral problems before you turned 15?

No, I don’t think so. I wasn’t getting into serious trouble or anything like that before 15.

I mean, I’m sure I had normal kid moments, but nothing I’d call significant behavioral problems. At least not that I remember. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like there's a part of you that's observing your impulsive actions, but not controlling them?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed it that way. Like, I can sometimes think afterward, “Why did I do that?” but in the moment I don’t really feel like there’s a separate part of me watching it happen.

I don’t know if that makes sense. I don’t want to overstate it if it’s not what you mean.
Did you often get into physical fights or bully others when you were younger?

No, not really. I wasn’t the kind of kid who got into fights or picked on people.

I mean, maybe there were little arguments or normal school stuff, but I don’t remember bullying anyone or being physically aggressive. I hope that’s what you mean.
Is there something specific about the late-night cutover incident that you're avoiding talking about?

I guess… yes, a little. I don’t mean to be difficult about it.

I just try not to go near that part of the building if I can help it. I’ll take the longer way around, or avoid that floor unless I absolutely have to. And when people start talking about the contractor or the cutover, I kind of shut it down or change the subject.

It’s probably not the best way to handle it, but it’s what I’ve been doing.
Do you think your impulsive behaviors are part of a long-standing pattern of how you interact with the world, rather than a response to a specific stressful event?

No… I don’t think it’s a long-standing pattern. At least, I really hope it doesn’t come across that way.

I came in because I’ve started doing things that scare me a little, like walking out in the middle of deployments or driving around late at night with no real plan. That’s… not how I’ve ever handled stress before. Usually I’m pretty controlled, maybe too controlled.

So I think it feels more tied to what happened than just “how I am,” if that makes sense.
